metadata.title: Chip Stocks Fall on AI Regulation Fears

content.text:
Last Updated:
Updated 16 hours ago
Chip Stocks Fall on AI Regulation Fears
Nvidia isn’t the only chipmaker feeling a post-midterms chill. Chips stocks took a bath Thursday as the market digested a wave of election wins by critics of AI and data centers. Qualcomm’s weak earnings report contributed to the carnage.
Nvidia’s biggest one-day drop since January 2025—its shares fell 9.3% to $181.60—was enough to erase all its year-to-date gains. Rival Advanced Micro Devices, fresh off an impressive earnings report this week, snapped a two-day winning streak, falling 17% to $404.40.
Other big names in the chips space, including Broadcom (-10%), Micron (-17%), Qualcomm (-9.5%) and Intel (-6.9%) saw big declines as well. Marvell and Lumentum, two other companies that design chips and network connectivity hardware and had announced an $80 billion merger this week, were slammed by double-digit percentage declines. Both companies have lost about half their market values in the past month.
